hens_rule_text: Up to 10 fowl (chickens counted together with rabbits/rodents) on the first half acre or less of a lot, with more allowed on larger lots and no limit at 2.5 acres or more. Arizona state law (A.R.S. 9-462.12) separately guarantees at least 6 hens on any single-family lot of half an acre or less.
permit_notes: No coop permit is required under Mesa City Code Sec. 8-6-21.
setback_notes: Sources describe an enclosure setback of about 40 ft and a coop setback of about 75 ft from any other residence; other secondary sources cite a simpler 20 ft figure. The exact distances could not be confirmed against the code text itself.
coop_rules: Enclosures must be kept sanitary and fowl must not be allowed to run loose or create a noise disturbance.
zoning_notes: Roosters are allowed as long as they do not create a noise disturbance; a substantiated noise complaint can require the rooster's removal. Arizona's A.R.S. 9-462.12 (2024) separately bars the city from banning up to 6 hens on a detached single-family lot of half an acre or less, regardless of the local fowl-or-rodent count rule.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Mesa City Code Sec. 8-6-21 (Fowl, Rodents & Livestock)

sources.name: coopcraftguide.com, Can You Have Chickens in Mesa, Arizona?
Az Chickens, Arizona Chicken Regulations City-by-City Guide

research_notes: Mesa's own municipal code page could not be opened or reached via search extract with the exact section text; the 10-fowl/half-acre rule and code section (8-6-21) are consistent across secondary chicken-law sites, but the setback distance is disputed between sources (40/75 ft vs 20 ft) and could not be resolved. State law A.R.S. 9-462.12 independently guarantees a 6-hen floor.
